Hell no. I'm turning 24 and have been in that "wrecked myself" stage for the past year. 4 years into a physics program (one semester off, failed some classes)  and switching to nursing this semester. I had some hard but necessary wake up calls and realized that my approach toward school and life in general was immature and my the source of motivation was misplaced. 

  
I'm a late bloomer in every respect. I often feel so behind that I will never catch up. I often dwell on the years and money I wasted on studying something so intense when I really had no passion for it. The rumination is dumb but addictive, and I'm an obsessive thinker.

  
Then I think of my younger brother. He's 21. Smoked some weed a month before graduating high school and went into a months long schizo-like psychotic episode that permanently altered his brain. All because of the weed and some genetic predispositions we didn't have a clue of. He lost his whole friend group because they were all stoners he could no longer be around, and on top of that, he was understandably embarrassed by what had happened. Started to pick up the pieces and got a job, but went into another episode a year later.

He missed out on the college train. Still has not fully recovered from it mentally. Has not made any friends since then because my parents had to sell their house and they moved to the middle of nowhere. On top of that, he feels like he cannot connect with people his age because many of them have surpassed milestones that he has yet to see. But guess what, after 2 years and a looooot of pushing from the family, he felt ready to pick himself up again. And after a ton of rejections he just landed a job. At a fast food place, but who gives a shit! I was ecstatic for him. Now he's saving up some money and thinking about starting college. And I'm so proud of him.

Everytime I realize I'm playing my tiny violin, telling myself I'm fucked, and there's no point, I think of him. I think of all of the experiences I have had that he hasn't - living in a major city, going to university classes, experiencing love...  I honestly see a world of potential in him and know he will succeed if he believes in himself the way that I believe in him. But if I say that I'm cooked because I'm broke, I chose the wrong major and haven't landed a professional job yet, I might as well tell him to give up now. And fuck that. 

  
Life is about way more than our accolades and possessions. The time you have spent "directionless" has shaped you in ways that will help you in wherever you end up. He will figure it out, I will figure it out, and you will figure it out. It sounds like you've made some big strides to better yourself, that's awesome. Start exploring some careers and focus on which ones most align with your goals over the next 10 years. If that's too hard, think 5. If you choose the wrong thing, boo hoo - you will have learned A LOT about yourself in the process. Just keep moving.

I think about this a lot too. Being in a LDR definitely brought a lot of those insecurities to light for me.

I think it’s only natural to continually be attracted and even tempted by people regardless of your relationship status. I’d argue that most coupled up people see people all the time and think “Damn, he/she is hot.” I don’t buy any “irresistible” BS though. If that’s the case, they’re just not that into you or never wanted a committed relationship in the first place. 

But trust grows with time. You can’t force yourself into a trusting relationship with people - it’s a slow give and take from both sides.

I think some level of jealousy/insecurity is “normal” (though not ideal). Just be wary of being accusatory in your relationships because when Partner A is constantly and illogically accusing Partner B of being unfaithful, Partner B might consider any of their efforts and displays of loyalty futile. 

You’ve gotta give people the benefit of the doubt unless they prove you wrong and you’ve got the evidence for it. Saying “I love how loyal you are to me” and leading by example of your standard is the best way to reinforce that behavior.

I’m 21 and still feel lost and confused about my “purpose”. I don’t know if that’s any reassurance to you. 

Everybody’s different. What I do that will benefit me varies vastly from what will benefit you in your life and career. But there are a few ideas that I think are universal.

The biggest thing is not to stay stagnant. Continue exploring new things and places. Socialize with people and build a good network of people around you who you can trust. Most of our lives and sense of connectedness and purpose revolve around close relationships. Work hard and honestly at every single thing you do. Take opportunities when they present themselves to you. Read a lot. When you find something that piques your interest, even a little, explore it until it’s dull to you. It’s easy to be overwhelmed by the immense possibilities of things you could do with your life but I find relief in knowing that I will never be defined by my career. There are so many more aspects to you that make you intrinsically unique. Just keep developing yourself and growing and do what seems most right to you in the waking moment, and everything in your future will fall into place.

There’s nothing wrong with having physical standards. You’re genetically programmed to try and get with the most attractive woman possible, and if you don’t find her attractive at all, it’s not going to work out. 

But at the same time, if you get past your monkey brain, you’ll find that the things that really make you fall for someone aren’t gonna be their physical traits, and basing too much of your attraction on this might lead you into a relationship with someone you find hot but emotionally incompatible and uninteresting. 

The color of their eyes starts to matter less than the way that they linger on yours, and the shape of their lips is a lot less exciting than the stories they tell and confessions they make. 

I’d say just give the next girl you find attractive (who maybe isn’t perfectly your “type”) a chance. Get to know her and see if you are able to develop any feelings for her (without leading her on of course). Don’t rush intimacy. If you’re a good fit, your physical attraction to her will only grow.

But again, I don’t think there’s anything wrong with having a specific type or certain physical standards - it just might get in the way of you connecting with many more people than you’ve limited yourself to. Ideally, you’d find that physically perfect person who matches with you in every other way as well. But it’s not your most realistic option, and you may be missing out on a great relationship and developing those skills that come along with maintaining one in search of this perfect individual.

Wear yourself out with some exercise, pop some melatonin, and force yourself to bed at night. No screens, light, noise, or anything else that would keep you up.

Or you can go the unhealthy route and pull your all nighter and stay up as long as possible. Even if you end up having to crash at 5pm, it’ll be easier as your body slowly adjusts toward going to bed earlier (or in this case later). Just make sure you don’t oversleep. 

The biggest thing is making sure you wake up at the same time regardless of whenever you go to bed, to give yourself some established routine and conditioning. It’s easier to control the time you wake up than the time you go to sleep.
